literature.headline_en: Underdiagnosed bacteremia in Marburg virus disease calls for revised antibiotic strategies.
literature.lead_en: A systematic review finds bacteremia occurs in Marburg virus disease at rates comparable to other high-consequence viral infections, but its clinical significance remains unclear.
key_findings_en: Sixteen cases of bacteremia were reported among Marburg virus disease patients, detected a median of 11 days after symptom onset [10.1093/ofid/ofag404].
Bacteremia was associated with sepsis features, yet mortality among coinfected patients did not differ from those without bacteremia [10.1093/ofid/ofag404].
Empiric antibiotics like ceftriaxone showed limited predicted activity against most bloodstream isolates, highlighting the need for optimized antimicrobial strategies [10.1093/ofid/ofag404].
The study underscores the lack of standardized bacterial diagnostic protocols in Marburg virus disease management.
Findings emphasize the urgency of prospective studies to define bacteremia's true incidence and clinical impact in Marburg virus disease.
literature.trend_or_risk_en: Despite bacteremia being documented in Marburg virus disease, its clinical significance remains uncertain, risking both overuse and underuse of antibiotics in outbreak settings.
literature.caveats_en: Evidence relies on case reports and cohort studies with heterogeneous diagnostic methods, limiting generalizability and causal inference.
literature.brief_en: Systematic review reveals bacteremia in Marburg virus disease, but standardized diagnostics and clinical significance remain unresolved.

papers.title: Bacterial infection in Ebola virus disease, Marburg virus disease, Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever, and Lassa fever
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Concern for bacterial coinfection in patients with high consequence viral infections (HCVIs) has made the empiric antibiotic administration the standard of care. However, the incidence, microbiology, and clinical significance of bacterial coinfection in HCVIs remain unclear. Methods We conducted a systematic review of case reports, cohort studies, and cross-sectional analyses describing bacterial coinfection in Ebola virus disease (EVD), Marburg virus disease (MVD), Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever (CCHF), and Lassa fever (LF). Data were extracted on study design, setting, diagnostic methods, pathogens, antibiotic use, and outcomes. Results Thirty publications met inclusion criteria. Bacteremia was most commonly reported among patients with CCHF (n = 46), followed by EVD (n = 16), MVD (n = 16), and LF (n = 2). Of 27 EVD patients treated outside Africa, seven (26%) had bacterial coinfection. Across HCVIs, bacteremia was detected a median of 11 days after symptom onset (range 0–23) and was associated with features of sepsis. Pathogens included enteric flora, healthcare-associated organisms, opportunistic pathogens, and zoonotic bacteria—most notably Brucella spp. Ceftriaxone was the most common empiric antibiotic but is predicted to have activity against a minority of bloodstream isolates. Mortality among coinfected patients with EVD or MVD was similar to those without bacterial coinfection, whereas coinfected CCHF patients had higher mortality than those without coinfection (15.5%; 95% CI 8.0–25.9% vs 5.7%; 95% CI 5.1–6.4%). Conclusions Despite being a major concern driving empiric antibiotic use, bacterial coinfection in HCVIs remains poorly described, precluding determination of its incidence or clinical significance. Prospective studies with standardized protocols for bacterial diagnosis and characterization of antimicrobial resistance are needed to guide antimicrobial strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to clarify the incidence, microbiology, and clinical significance of bacterial coinfection in patients with high consequence viral infections (HCVIs), including Marburg virus disease (MVD), as concern for bacterial coinfection has driven empiric antibiotic administration despite unclear evidence.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A systematic review of case reports, cohort studies, and cross-sectional analyses was conducted to describe bacterial coinfection in MVD and other HCVIs, with data extracted on study design, setting, diagnostic methods, pathogens, antibiotic use, and outcomes.
analysis.methods: The review included studies describing bacterial coinfection in MVD, with data extraction focused on pathogens, diagnostic methods, antibiotic use, and outcomes, though specific protocols for bacterial diagnosis were not standardized across studies.
analysis.main_results: Among patients with MVD, 16 cases of bacteremia were reported; across all HCVIs, bacteremia was detected a median of 11 days after symptom onset and was associated with features of sepsis, with mortality among coinfected MVD patients similar to those without bacterial coinfection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that bacterial coinfection in HCVIs, including MVD, remains poorly described, precluding determination of its incidence or clinical significance, despite being a major concern driving empiric antibiotic use.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings highlight the need for prospective studies with standardized protocols for bacterial diagnosis and characterization of antimicrobial resistance to guide antimicrobial strategies in MVD and other HCVIs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is limited by the lack of standardized protocols for bacterial diagnosis and characterization of antimicrobial resistance across studies, with the reliance on case reports and cohort studies introducing potential bias and confounding.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review investigated bacterial coinfection in high consequence viral infections (HCVIs), including Marburg virus disease (MVD). Among MVD patients, 16 cases of bacteremia were reported, with bacteremia detected a median of 11 days after symptom onset and associated with sepsis features. Mortality in coinfected MVD patients was similar to non-coinfected cases. The study found that bacterial coinfection in HCVIs remains poorly characterized, despite driving empiric antibiotic use. Pathogens included enteric flora, healthcare-associated organisms, and opportunistic bacteria, with ceftriaxone being the most common empiric antibiotic but predicted to have limited activity against bloodstream isolates. The authors emphasize the need for prospective studies with standardized diagnostic protocols to guide antimicrobial strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在阐明 发病率、微生物学和细菌合并感染对包括 马尔堡病毒病 (MVD) 在内的高后果病毒感染 (HCVI) 患者的临床意义,因为尽管证据不明确,但对细菌合并感染的担忧推动了经验性抗生素给药。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对 病例报告、队列研究 研究和横断面分析进行了系统回顾,以描述 MVD 和其他 HCVI 中的细菌合并感染,并提取了有关研究设计、设置、诊断方法、病原体、抗生素使用和结果的数据。
elements_zh.methods: 该综述包括描述 MVD 中细菌共感染的研究,数据提取侧重于病原体、诊断方法、抗生素使用和结果,尽管细菌 诊断 的具体方案在研究中并未标准化。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 MVD 患者中,报告了 16 例菌血症;在所有 HCVI 中,菌血症在症状出现后平均 11 天被发现,并且与败血症的特征相关,合并感染的 MVD 患者中的 死亡率 与没有细菌合并感染的患者相似。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,HCVI 中的细菌合并感染(包括 MVD)仍然缺乏描述,无法确定其 发病率 或临床意义,尽管这是推动经验性抗生素使用的一个主要问题。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调需要对细菌 诊断 和抗菌药物耐药性的标准化方案进行前瞻性研究,以指导 MVD 和其他 HCVI 的抗菌策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于缺乏细菌 诊断 的标准化方案和跨研究的抗菌药物耐药性特征,证据强度受到限制,并且依赖 病例报告 和 队列研究 研究引入了潜在的偏差和混杂因素。

Alves Human brain organoids reveal how Ebola virus establishes persistent infection within the immune-privileged environment of the central nervous system. The idea of immune privilege has reshaped our understanding of how the immune system is regulated across tissues. It is viewed as a state of selective immune tolerance characterized by tissue- and organ-specific immune regulation. Classic examples include the central nervous sys- tem (CNS), eyes and testes, where immune surveillance is present but constrained. These sites maintain a highly regulated immunological milieu through cellular barriers, local immunoregulatory mediators and context-dependent modulation of antigen presentation. While this restrained inflammatory tone is essential to preserve the function and integrity of indispensable tissues, it comes at a cost: the same features that limit immunopathology can also reduce pathogen clearance. As a result, immune-privileged niches may be co-opted by pathogens as long-term reservoirs and enable persistence despite systemic immune surveillance. Understanding how viruses exploit these specialized envi- ronments is therefore critical for defining the mechanisms underlying chronic infection and relapse. Numerous studies have characterized viral replication dynamics, transmission and evolution during acute Ebola virus (EBOV) infection. However, increasing evidence indicates that EBOV can persist during the chronic phase, with ongoing viral replication in survivors sup- porting the concept that persistence represents an active infection Check for updates Immune-privileged CNS • Restrained inflammation • Cellular barriers (for example, BBB and choroid plexus) • Antigen drainage (glymphatics and meningeal lymphatics) • Limited immune surveillance EBOV persistence in the brain Virus exploits immune privilege to establish long-term infection The hidden cost Chronic neuroinflammation Type I IFNs and inflammatory mediators Neuron Astrocyte Microglia Oligodendrocyte Defective viral genomes Viral evolution Persistent reservoirs Neuronal dysfunction and injury Fig. 1 | Immune privilege as a double-edged sword during EBOV persistence in the CNS. The CNS maintains a tightly regulated immune environment that limits inflammation and preserves tissue integrity. In human brain organoids, EBOV infects multiple neural cell types, including neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and microglia, via viral spread through budding and direct cell-to-cell transmission. Persistent infection is associated with viral evolution and accumulation of defective viral genomes, mechanisms thought to favour chronic low-level replication. In parallel, activated microglia produce pro- inflammatory mediators and type I interferons (IFNs) that may drive chronic neuroinflammation and neuronal injury. BBB, blood–brain barrier. nature microbiology News & views within immune-privileged reservoirs1. Among these niches, the CNS has emerged as a particularly clinically relevant site, as studies in non- human primates have demonstrated that replication-competent EBOV can remain in the brain after clearance from the periphery, leading to fatal relapses2. Yet the mechanisms underlying EBOV persistence in the human CNS remain poorly understood, leaving key questions unanswered regarding the neural cell populations that support long- term infection and the associated host responses. In this issue of Nature Microbiology, Widerspick and colleagues3 provide mechanistic insights on how orthoebolaviruses exploit the CNS’s immune-privileged status to establish long-term persistence. The authors developed a human brain organoid model that enables long-term analysis of orthoebolavirus infection in the human neural tissue and tested EBOV (species Orthoebolavirus zairense), Sudan virus (species Orthoebolavirus sudanense), Reston virus (species Orthoe- bolavirus restonense), and a related filovirus, Marburg virus (species Orthomarburgvirus marburgense). In these organoids, they show that EBOV can persist for up to 120 days within diverse neural cell types, including neurons, astrocytes, microglia and oligodendrocytes. This persistence, referring to the continued presence of infectious virus or viral genetic material beyond the acute phase of infection, suggests that EBOV can establish a sustained reservoir within human neural tissue. Mechanistically, the study shows that EBOV persistence relies on both canonical viral budding and direct cell-to-cell transmission through actin-dependent cellular projections and syncytia formation. Cell-to- cell spread is recognized as a potential mechanism of immune evasion, allowing viruses to disseminate while potentially reducing exposure to soluble immune mediators4. Within highly interconnected neural tissue, this mode of spread may be advantageous, as shown by our recent work demonstrating that monkeypox virus exploits neuronal connectivity to propagate while limiting immune exposure5. Widerspick and colleagues observed that long-term persistence of EBOV was associated with ongoing viral evolution together with the accumulation of defective viral genomes. Defective viral genomes are increasingly recognized as regulators of persistent infection because they can attenuate cytopathic replication while allowing for minimal levels of viral activity. By interfering with replication of full-length viral genomes, defective viral genomes have been proposed to modulate viral replication and host responses, potentially reducing cytopathic effects and contributing to persistence6. Importantly, the study iden- tifies marked cell type-specific differences in the host response to persistent EBOV infection. Whereas infected astrocytes remained comparatively quiescent, microglia mounted robust pro-inflammatory and type I interferon responses, identifying these cells as likely drivers of the chronic neuroinflammation associated with EBOV persistence. This observation reinforces the concept that immune privilege may support long-term viral maintenance while allowing inflammatory responses to emerge once local immune activation is engaged (Fig. 1). Similar patterns have been observed in other neurotropic viral infections. Replication-competent Zika virus, for example, can persist in the brains of surviving mice for more than 1 year within inflamma- tory foci enriched in activated microglia and astrocytes, where viral persistence is associated with chronic inflammation and neuronal injury7. More broadly, persistent viral reservoirs represent one of sev- eral proposed mechanisms contributing to post-acute sequelae of infection, including long COVID, in which sustained immune activation may result from a combination of viral persistence, immune dysregula- tion and other host factors8,9. Whether the mechanisms of CNS persis- tence identified for EBOV are conserved among other Orthoebolavirus species such as Bundibugyo virus — the driving pathogen of the current Ebola disease outbreak — remains unclear. Bundibugyo virus has shown evidence of CNS involvement in animal models, with viral antigen and RNA detected in CNS-associated tissues10,11, and long-term neurological sequelae reported in human survivors12. However, whether Bundibugyo virus establishes CNS persistence through similar cellular tropism and host–virus interactions remains unknown. Comparative studies will be required to determine whether CNS persistence represents a conserved feature across all orthoebolaviruses and to define the viral and host determinants that enable long-term infection within neural tissue. Although brain organoids provide a valuable platform to investi- gate EBOV persistence in human neural tissue, they remain a simplified representation of the CNS and do not fully recapitulate the complex immune, barrier and cellular interactions that shape viral persistence within the intact CNS. Consequently, caution is warranted when extrapo- lating these findings to human disease. This is particularly relevant given that the CNS maintains selective communication with the peripheral immune system through structures such as the glymphatic system and meningeal lymphatic vessels, which facilitate antigen clearance and immune cross-talk between the brain and peripheral lymphoid organs. The meninges, choroid plexus and perivascular spaces are also recognized as neuroimmune hubs that coordinate immune surveillance, antigen presentation and leukocyte trafficking13. Addressing these ques- tions will be essential to determine whether EBOV persistence reflects escape from immune surveillance or an active adaptation to the CNS environment. Future organoid models incorporating cellular barriers, vascular components and peripheral immune cells will help determine how these virus–host interactions are shaped by neuroimmune com- munication and how EBOV establishes and maintains CNS reservoirs. They may also clarify whether microglia promote or restrict persistence and whether viral evolution within the CNS contributes to relapse or transmission. Collectively, these next-generation human brain models will provide a framework to investigate the mechanisms governing viral persistence in the CNS in a more physiologically relevant context. papers.title: Marburg Virus: A Looming Threat Nigeria Cannot Ignore.
papers.abstract: To the Editor: high population density, and concurrent Lassa fever and Mpox burdens make preparedness a national imperative [7]. The recent cross-sectional assessment by Oisakede et al. [8] offers empirical confirmation of this vulnerability. The study, conducted among 216 healthcare workers at Nigeria's national viral haemorrhagic fever reference centre (Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital), revealed that only 19 % of doctors and 10 % of nurses had received formal MVD training, and less than half felt adequately protected by personal protective equipment (PPE). Confidence in hospital readiness was significantly lower among doctors (32.5 %) than nurses (65.6 %), indicating institutional and role-specific disparities in outbreak preparedness.These empirical findings from Oisakede et al. [8] and the regional evidence base reveal a clear preparedness gap. While Nigeria benefits from a national Lassa fever infrastructure, this platform is yet to be fully extended to filoviruses like Marburg. The 2026 data provide a measurable baseline for monitoring progress and justify targeted capacity-building funding within the National Action Plan for Health Security (2026-2030). Preparedness is thus not merely theoretical; it demands investment in people, protocols and platforms. Leveraging the Oisakede et al. [8] evidence for policy advocacy strengthens the argument that Nigeria must institutionalise training, simulation, and infrastructure before the next filovirus crisis arrives. papers.title: Digital Health for Pandemic Preparedness: A Critical Review of Innovations, Equity Gaps, and Governance in Infectious Disease Surveillance
papers.abstract: Context: Recent infectious disease emergencies, including SARS-CoV-2, mpox (2022 - 2024), highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) in US dairy cattle (2024 - 2025), and the Marburg virus in Rwanda (2024), have strained traditional surveillance systems. Digital health has been proposed as a paradigm shift; however, most reviews have focused on diagnostic accuracy while neglecting equity and governance. Evidence Acquisition: We conducted a structured thematic narrative review of peer-reviewed and grey literature published from January 2010 to March 2025, reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from February 5 to 18, 2025. Search keywords combined three concept blocks: (1) Digital-health technologies (artificial intelligence, machine learning, mHealth, eHealth, telemedicine, electronic health records, wearables, wastewater surveillance, genomic surveillance, natural-language processing); (2) infectious diseases (outbreak, pandemic, epidemic, COVID-19, Ebola, Zika, mpox, influenza, antimicrobial resistance, Marburg); and (3) public-health functions (surveillance, detection, forecasting, contact tracing, governance, equity). Full Boolean syntax is provided. Records were deduplicated in EndNote X20 and screened by 2 blinded reviewers in Rayyan (Cohen κ = 0.81). Empirical studies were appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool 2018, and reviews were appraised using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. The synthesis followed Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis and was interpreted through sociotechnical systems and data justice lenses. Results: Of 1498 records, 142 studies met the inclusion criteria; 48% (69/142) were rated as high quality. The evidence base was heavily skewed regionally (high-income countries [HICs], 41%; sub-Saharan Africa or South Asia, 19%). No technology was universally superior. Artificial intelligence (AI) studies were concentrated in HICs (18/32, 56%), whereas short-message-service (SMS) mHealth studies were concentrated in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs; 15/25, 60%). Recurring barriers included algorithmic bias, fragmented interoperability, donor-dependent sustainability, and slow benefit-sharing of pathogen data with LMICs. Conclusions: Across 142 included studies the synthesis supports a measured conclusion: Digital health is necessary but not sufficient for pandemic preparedness. The patterns most consistently observed in the evidence — regional skew, recurring governance failures, donor-dependent sustainability, and design choices that determine equity outcomes — together indicate that equity, sustainability, and accountability are constituents of effectiveness rather than obstacles to it. The binding constraint is increasingly political and institutional will rather than analytic uncertainty.

analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在 1498 项记录中,142 项研究符合纳入标准,其中 48% 被评为高质量。证据基础存在地区偏差,41% 来自高收入国家,19% 来自撒哈拉以南非洲或南亚。没有一种技术是普遍优越的。人工智能研究集中在高收入国家,而短信移动医疗研究则集中在中低收入国家。在纳入的研究中,数字健康对于大流行防范来说是必要的,但还不够。公平、可持续性和问责制是有效性的组成部分,而不是障碍。

papers.title: UNDERSTANDING LIPID-PROTEIN INTERACTIONS IN THE CONTEXT OF EBOLA AND MARBURG VIRUSES TO UNCOVER UNDERLYING MECHANISMS OF DISEASE PROGRESSION
papers.abstract: Protein-lipid interactions are fundamental regulators of membrane-associated protein structure and function, thus influencing processes involving both viral life cycle and normal cellular functioning. Therefore, these interactions become important in understanding the underlying principles of progression of multitude of diseases. Viral matrix proteins are a fantastic model system to study these processes because these proteins rely heavily on host cellular membranes to coordinate trafficking and assembly. in this thesis, we have investigated the molecular mechanisms of membrane association of various proteins, with a focus on Ebola and Marburg virus matrix protein VP40.These viruses cause a highly fatal hemorrhagic fever and there is a dire need for finding ways to combat them, hence, learning how these viruses use their proteins to exploit host cellular membranes is a very important step in the battle against them. This knowledge has been further extended to the human parainfluenza virus 3 (HPIV-3) matrix protein M and the human protein ceramide kinase (CERK) to examine how they interact with certain lipids.With the help of mutagenesis, cellular assays and biochemical and biophysical approaches, this study has uncovered the essential roles of membrane binding residues of VP40 in coordinating multiple stages of viral life cycle. This has also identified critical residues in both proteins and indicated a difference in sensitivity towards mutations. We have also identified lipid binding modes of HPIV-3 M and CERK.Overall, this thesis highlights the importance of protein-lipid interactions as determinants of membrane-associated protein function and reveals how distinct molecular structure can achieve similar biological functions. These findings advance our understanding of viral assembly as well as a broader insight into lipid-dependent cellular processes.

The findings reveal how distinct molecular structures achieve similar functions through lipid interactions, advancing knowledge of viral assembly and cellular processes. This work provides a scientific foundation for developing countermeasures against these highly fatal hemorrhagic fevers by targeting viral exploitation of host membranes.

papers.abstract_zh: 蛋白质-脂质相互作用是膜相关蛋白质结构和功能的基本调节剂,从而影响涉及病毒生命周期和正常细胞功能的过程。因此,这些相互作用对于理解多种疾病进展的基本原理变得很重要。病毒基质蛋白是研究这些过程的绝佳模型系统,因为这些蛋白严重依赖 宿主 细胞膜来协调运输和组装。在本论文中,我们研究了各种蛋白质的膜关联的分子机制,重点是埃博拉病毒和马尔堡病毒基质蛋白VP40。这些病毒引起高度致命的出血热,迫切需要找到对抗它们的方法,因此,了解这些病毒如何利用它们的蛋白质来利用马尔堡病毒细胞膜是对抗它们的非常重要的一步。这一知识已进一步扩展到人副流感病毒 3 (HPIV-3) 基质蛋白 M 和人蛋白神经酰胺激酶 (CERK),以检查它们如何与某些脂质相互作用。在诱变、细胞分析以及生化和生物物理方法的帮助下,本研究揭示了 VP40 膜结合残基在协调病毒生命周期多个阶段中的重要作用。这还鉴定了两种蛋白质中的关键残基,并表明对 突变 的敏感性存在差异。我们还确定了 HPIV-3 M 和 CERK 的脂质结合模式。总体而言,本文强调了蛋白质-脂质相互作用作为膜相关蛋白质功能决定因素的重要性,并揭示了不同的分子结构如何实现相似的生物学功能。这些发现增进了我们对病毒组装的理解以及对脂质依赖性细胞过程的更广泛的了解。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现强调了不同的分子结构如何通过蛋白质-脂质相互作用实现相似的生物学功能,从而增进对病毒组装和脂质依赖性细胞过程的理解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些见解为制定策略通过针对 宿主 细胞膜的利用来对抗埃博拉和 马尔堡病毒 引起的高度致命的出血热提供了基础。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据强度中等,因为它侧重于分子机制,没有直接的临床应用或大规模人群数据,尽管它提供了详细的生化和生物物理分析。
